newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung in finance JV with US, Japan firms.
newsitem.headline: Samsung in finance JV with US, Japan firms.

text.p: Samsung Group said on Monday it has signed an agreement to set up an investment trust management firm in South Korea in a joint venture with JP Morgan Investment Management and Japan's Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
A Samsung statement said the joint venture was expected to contribute to the domestic financial industry's growth by introducing advanced financial practices to the local market.
Samsung and the JP Morgan & Co unit will each invest 30 percent of the joint venture's capital of 30 billion won, and Yamaichi will have 10 percent, a Samsung statement said.
Samsung's stake will be divided into 16.7 percent for Samsung Securities Co, 10 percent for unlisted Samsung Life Insurance Co and 3.3 percent for Samsung Fire and Marine Insurance Co, it said.
South Korea's Samyang Merchant Banking Corp will hold another 10 percent stake and the remining 20 percent will be equally shared by four domestic commercial banks, the statement said.
The four are Daegu Bank, Commercial Bank of Korea, Hanil Bank and Industrial Bank of Korea.
The joint venture, tentatively named Samsung JP Morgan Investment Trust Management Co, was scheduled to be established in December, the statement said.
